# 🪄 Intelligent UI for DeepSeek Harness English | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [中文](README.zh.md) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-Plugin-emerald.svg)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) > **Turn LLM responses into live, interactive mini-apps directly inside DeepSeek Harness.** **Intelligent UI** is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (Desktop & Web UI) inspired by ChatGPT's Intelligent UI and Claude Artifacts. Instead of generating static walls of text, the model writes markdown embedded with interactive component tags, reactive expressions, and beautiful Mermaid diagrams. The chat interface renders them in-place in real time as the response streams in. --- ## 📸 Screenshots | 🧮 Interactive Cost Simulator | ⚖️ Interactive Tech Stack Comparison | | :---: | :---: | | | |

🎨 Themed Mermaid Diagrams with Rounded Nodes & Semantic Role Colors

--- ## ✨ Key Features - ⚡ **Real-Time Interactive Mini-Apps**: Sliders, number inputs, dropdowns, and toggles recompute formulas, statistics, and charts instantly inside your browser—no backend round-trips needed. - 📊 **Rich UI Component Library**: Over 20 built-in components including KPI tiles (`stat`), bar/line/pie charts (`chart`), responsive layouts (`box`, `row`, `grid`), progress bars, data tables, badges, and segmented controls. - 🎨 **Beautiful Themed Diagrams**: Automatically transforms ` ```mermaid ` fences into styled diagrams with rounded cards, dark/light theme harmony, and hierarchy-aware typography. - 🔁 **Bidirectional Interaction**: Action buttons (`GenUI.issueNewTurn(...)`) let you send configured values back to the agent as your next prompt with a single click. - 🧠 **Context-Aware Triggering**: The model intelligently uses UI only when helpful (e.g., calculations, comparisons, workflows) and answers simple questions in clean plain text. - 🔒 **Secure by Design**: Expressions execute inside a sandboxed AST interpreter without `eval`, DOM access, or network permissions. Form state stays strictly within your local browser session. --- ## 🚀 Installation Requires **DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x** or later (Desktop app or `dsh web`). ### Option 1: Web UI / Desktop App (Easiest) 1. Open DeepSeek Harness. 2. Navigate to **Plugins** → Click **Add plugin**. 3. Enter either package name or repository URL: ``` @rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui ``` or ``` https://github.com/rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui ``` 4. Click **Install**. The plugin is ready to use immediately without restarting! ### Option 2: CLI Installation Run the following command in your terminal: ```sh # For Desktop app profile (make sure to quit Desktop first): dsh plugin --profile desktop add @rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui # For Web server profile: dsh plugin --profile web add @rakutek/dsh-intelligent-ui ``` > **Note**: To temporarily return to plain-text replies, simply toggle off the plugin in **Plugins**. --- ## 💡 Example Prompts to Try Once installed, prompt the model naturally with questions that benefit from interactivity: - **Simulators & Estimations**: > *"Create a SaaS pricing simulator where I can adjust team seats and billing frequency (monthly vs. annual) and see the discount impact."* - **Product Comparisons**: > *"Compare MacBook Pro M3, ThinkPad X1 Carbon, and Dell XPS 13 for battery life, weight, price, and developer workflows with interactive filters."* - **Workflow & Architecture Diagrams**: > *"Draw a flowchart showing how a GitHub pull request goes through CI checks, code review, and deployment."* - **Financial & Planning Calculators**: > *"Build a mortgage repayment calculator with loan amount, interest rate slider, and amortization chart."* --- ## 🛠️ How It Works (What the Model Writes) The plugin injects concise instructions into the system prompt. The model writes standard Markdown enhanced with JSX-like component tags and reactive state declarations: ```md {@body const [seats, setSeats] = useState(25)} {@body const [price, setPrice] = useState(1200)} Team Plan Estimator ``` ### Supported Components & Syntax | Category | Available Elements | |---|---| | **Layout & Structure** | ``, ``, ``, ``, `` | | **Typography & Data** | ``, `<text>`, `<caption>`, `<label>`, `<badge>`, `<icon>`, `<stat>`, `<progress>` | | **Tables & Collections**| `<table>`, `<table-row>`, `<table-cell>` | | **Data Visualization** | `<chart type="bar|line|pie|area" data={...}/>`, Themed Mermaid diagrams | | **Interactive Controls**| `<slider>`, `<input>`, `<checkbox>`, `<radio-group>`, `<radio>`, `<segmented-control>`, `<select>`, `<button>` | | **Expressions & Logic** | `{expression}`, `{#if condition}...{/if}`, `{#each item in list}...{/each}`, `{@body ...}` | --- ## 🛡️ Security & Privacy - **Sandboxed Execution**: Expressions are evaluated via a safe AST interpreter. There is no `eval()`, `new Function()`, access to `window`/`document`, or network fetch access. - **Local State Privacy**: Interactive input state is saved per message in your browser's local storage. Values are never sent to the model until you explicitly click an action button. - **Safe Resources**: External links open via DeepSeek Harness's native safe URL handler. External images only load from model-specified HTTPS URLs. --- ## 📋 Compatibility - **DeepSeek Harness**: `v0.2.0-rc.1` or later - **Tested Models**: Claude 3.5 Sonnet / 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4o / GPT-6.1, DeepSeek-V3 / R1 --- ## 📄 License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). Distributed client bundles package [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid) and [zod](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod). See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) for full licensing disclosures.

Use the same engine from the browser: - **Vocal Remover & Karaoke** — https://www.sonicaurastudio.com/tools/ai-vocal - **Multitrack Splitter (2/4/6 stems)** — https://www.sonicaurastudio.com/tools/vocal-separation ## Credits Processing uses credits. plugins.description: An eye-friendly green skin for DeepSeek Harness.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-leafy-skin

An eye-friendly green skin: a leafy palette layered over the official DSH web GUI theme, in a
light emerald and a dark mint variant.

> I wanted the effect of a Minecraft resource pack.

**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

## Screenshot

![Screenshot](show.png)

## Features

- **Layered greens** — a mist-green canvas, raised panels, and a deeper sidebar, with emerald
  accents in light mode and mint in dark, instead of one flat wash of green.
- **Comfortable by construction** — no pure white or pure black, a single green hue family, and
  all body text at WCAG AA (≥ 4.5:1).
- **Texture** — softer corner radii, green-tinted diffuse shadows, low-contrast hairlines, and
  glassy menu surfaces.
- **Details** — mint text selection, Inter / Noto Sans SC / Cascadia Code font stacks, slim
  scrollbars, and restrained hover and menu motion.
- **Tunable** — the palette is one commented table, a self-check script guards contrast, and the
  style layer has a single on/off switch.

## Install

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-leafy-skin
```

Restart DSH once afterwards so the profile recomposes. After that, colour edits only need a page
refresh (client changes hot-reload within about a second).

## Usage

Install the plugin and load the app. The skin layers itself over the active theme, so light, dark,
and follow-system each pick up their own variant automatically.

## Customize

- **Colours** — the `TOKENS` table in `lib/client.js`, grouped and commented by area.
- **Radii, shadows, fonts, motion** — the same file, plus the small style layer below it.
- **Palette only** — set `ENABLE_CSS_LAYER` to `false` in `lib/client.js` to drop the style layer
  entirely.
- **Check your work** — `node tools/check-palette.mjs` validates token shape, text and syntax
  contrast, and the style layer's three constraints.

## Uninstall

Any one of these, then restart DSH:

1. Comment out the `insert` entry in `cordis.patch.yml`;
2. Drop `dsh-leafy-skin` from `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`;
3. Run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-leafy-skin`.

## Known limitations

- The native window title bar belongs to the DSH desktop shell, not to this plugin, so it stays
  DSH grey for the instant before the page paints.
- Real see-through glass is impossible on Windows — the sidebar depth and translucent menus are
  colour layering, not blur through the window.
- Components hard-code font sizes and layout in hashed CSS modules, so this skin deliberately
  leaves them alone.

## Changelog

See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

## Contributing

Questions and suggestions are welcome as issues. Pull requests are not accepted.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: commit activity, contribution heatmap with shared selection, and a calibrated 72h release probability
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-tianyicui-monitor

[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-109%20passing-brightgreen)](#tests)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin. It adds a
sidebar entry showing a maintainer's commit activity and a **calibrated probability that a new DSH
version ships within 72 hours**.

Reads public GitHub data only. No credentials, no telemetry.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

---

## What it does

A row in the DSH sidebar, next to Plugins / MCP, opening a report:

- **Verdict** — a gauge with the 90% threshold drawn on the arc, and a verdict band
  (`release likely` / `watch` / `quiet`)
- **Totals** — commits in the main repo, commits across all public repos, GitHub contribution count
- **Timeline** — daily commits with release markers
- **Heatmap** — GitHub-style contribution grid
- **Model timeline** — DeepSeek model launches against DSH releases
- **Contributions** — daily GitHub contribution counts, private-activity days flagged
- **Evidence** — Brier / AUC / calibration error, and the hazard bucket behind the current number

Click any day on the timeline or the heatmap: both charts highlight it and a readout shows that
day's commit counts, whether a release landed, and which version.

## How the probability is derived

### 1. Predictors

Each hour is a sample. Two features are used, both known at that moment:

- **hours since the last release**
- **day of week**

Commit volume was tested and dropped: in a 24-hour window it carries no signal (0.99× the baseline).
Whether a release is *overdue* is what matters.

### 2. Hazard × weekday

Bucketed by hours since the last release, the empirical release rate rises steadily as a cycle ages:

| Hours since last release | P(release within 72h) |
|---|---|
| 0–6 h | 74.4% |
| 30–36 h | 64.0% |
| 48–60 h | 85.7% |
| 72–96 h | 97.0% |
| 96 h+ | 100% |

There is also a strong weekday effect — the team ships midweek, not on Fridays (Thursday 95.8% vs
Friday 54.7%). The two are combined on the odds scale:

```
logit P = logit(hazard[hours-since-last-release bucket])
        + log(weekday relative risk)
```

### 3. Calibration

A monotone (isotonic) curve is fitted to the model's own out-of-sample output, so the number shown
is the observed frequency rather than a raw score.

```
P_calibrated = isotonic(P_raw)
```

### 4. Why a 72-hour window

The probability that a release lands in the next **24 hours** tops out at **77.7%** (Wilson upper
bound 87.9%), so a 90% verdict is unreachable in that window. Over 72 hours it reaches **94.0%**,
which makes 90% a real, crossable line:

| Horizon | Base rate | Best achievable | Reaches 90%? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 h | 24.4% | 54.0% | no |
| 24 h | 43.1% | 77.7% | no |
| 48 h | 63.5% | 88.8% | no |
| **72 h** | **78.8%** | **94.0%** | **yes** |

(Base rate here is the unconditional release rate over the same window used for the horizon sweep;
the calibrated model's own fitted base rate over its training window is 82.1%.)

## Validation

Rolling-origin backtesting: refit every 6 hours on data strictly before the evaluation instant,
across 1,092 out-of-sample hours.

| Model | Brier ↓ | AUC ↑ | Log loss ↓ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Constant base rate | 0.1509 | 0.500 | 0.4819 |
| hazard × weekday | 0.1402 | 0.687 | 0.4451 |
| **+ isotonic calibration** | **0.1346** | **0.687** | **0.4426** |

Calibration error falls from 7.33 pp to **4.17 pp**.

The ≥90% verdict fires on 49.9% of hours and is followed by a release within 72 hours **92.7%** of
the time (Wilson 95% CI 90.2–94.6%).

> **Limitation:** the history contains only 37 independent release events, so the intervals are
> wide. The panel states this in its footer. Do not make important decisions from it.

## DeepSeek model releases

Model launches are shown as timeline context, **not** as a model input. Scoped to models published
since the DSH repository was created — including **V4-Flash-0731** and **V4-Pro-0813** — with dates
taken from Hugging Face model-card creation time.

Notable alignment: each of the three flagship launches *after* DSH's first public release was
followed by a DSH release within **0.5 days**.

| Model launch | Next DSH release |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-13 · V4-Pro-0813 | +0.2 d |
| 2026-08-31 · V4-Flash-Vision-Exp | +0.4 d |
| 2026-09-10 · V4.1-Flash | +0.5 d |

> With only three observations this is a pattern, not a measurable effect, and it is not evidence
> that a model launch *causes* a DSH release. The three earlier launches predate DSH's first release
> and cannot be compared at all. They are deliberately kept out of the probability model, both
> because n=3 cannot support a predictor and because the base rate already explains most of it.

## Install

```bash
npm test        # 109 tests
npm run build   # emits lib/client.js
```

Place the package under your DSH profile's `node_modules`, then append a loader entry to that
profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: tianyicui-monitor
      name: dsh-tianyicui-monitor
```

Restart DSH. `sync.sh` automates the copy:

```bash
DSH_CANON_DIR="$HOME/dsh-plugins/dsh-tianyicui-monitor" \
DSH_PROFILES="$HOME/.dsh/profiles/web" \
  ./sync.sh
```

## Data sources

| What | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Commits in the main repo | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits` |
| Releases | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases` |
| Commits across all public repos | `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contributors` |
| Contribution graph (includes private) | `https://github.com/users/{u}/contributions` |

An offline snapshot ships with the plugin so the panel always renders, then refreshes live.
Unauthenticated GitHub allows 60 requests/hour; the panel shows a countdown when that runs out.

Two notes on reading this data:

- **Unreadable is not zero.** `GET /user/repos` returns **401** unauthenticated, so private
  repositories cannot be counted. The panel reports `private repos visible: 0` and says why.
- **The contribution graph counts "contributions"** (commits + PRs + issues + reviews), **not
  commits**, so it is shown as a separate row and never summed with the commit totals. Its daily
  numbers do include private activity, because the account enables "include private contributions on
  my profile". GitHub returns only the count, never the repository.

A true commit count including private repos needs an authenticated GraphQL query
(`contributionsCollection.totalCommitContributions`).

## Tests

```bash
npm test
```

109 tests. `test/render.test.mjs` evaluates the built bundle and executes every component body
against real data; `test/contributions.test.mjs` parses a real captured page and asserts its daily
sum matches the total GitHub prints; `test/core.test.mjs` covers the analysis core and re-verifies
the model's own claims.

## Rebuilding the data

```bash
git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --shallow-since=2026-04-01 \
  --single-branch --branch master \
  https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git build/dsh-git

npm run data            # extract -> refit -> bundle
npm run repos           # per-repo commit scan
npm run contributions   # contribution graph
```

Every number above is reproducible with `node build/evaluate3.mjs` and
`node build/evaluate4.mjs`.

## Disclaimer

Not affiliated with or endorsed by DeepSeek or by `tianyicui`. It reads public GitHub data about a
public account. All trademarks belong to their owners.

MIT licensed.

plugins.description: 腾讯 WorkBuddy 接入 DeepSeek Harness 的 LLM 插件：浏览器 OAuth 登录、无需 API Key。Tencent WorkBuddy LLM provider plugin for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-llm-workbuddy-cn

**English** | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin for **Tencent WorkBuddy**.

Sign in through your browser — **no API key required** — and use WorkBuddy's own model list.

## Features

- **Browser OAuth sign-in** — authorize in a normal browser tab; no API key needed, ever. Sign in to either the China or the international site.
- **Full model catalog** — WorkBuddy's own models, with context windows, output caps, and credit multipliers; server-side additions and removals are picked up automatically.
- **Streaming chat** — responses stream in real time.
- **Tool calls** — function calling, with a clear error when a model does not support it.
- **Reasoning effort** — pick a thinking level for models that support one.
- **Image input** — attach images for vision-capable models (models without vision support may be routed to a different model by the server).
- **Usage indicator** — a quota bar in the Web UI sidebar for both personal and enterprise plans, with an optional custom cap and a configurable danger threshold.

## Compatibility

| Requirement | Version |
| --- | --- |
| DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) | `>= 0.1.7-rc.1` |

Web UI features such as the settings page, model picker, and usage indicator require the `web` profile.

## Install

Add the plugin to a dsh profile — the `web` profile backs the Web UI:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:wenh56884-wq/dsh-llm-workbuddy
```

The repository ships its compiled `lib/`, so a Git install needs no build step and no
dev dependencies. Installing from a source checkout works too:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-llm-workbuddy
```

## Sign in

Open **Settings → WorkBuddy** in the Web UI and pick a site: **Sign in (China)** for [www.workbuddy.cn](https://www.workbuddy.cn) or **Sign in (Intl)** for [www.workbuddy.ai](https://www.workbuddy.ai). The browser login opens in a new tab; the harness writes the credential automatically. No terminal needed.

The two sites are the same service on different hosts but hold **separate accounts** — one site's account does not work on the other — so the site is chosen per sign-in and recorded with the credential. Every later request goes to the host that issued it. To move to the other site, sign out and sign in again.

Alternatively, sign in from the terminal:

```bash
# A CLI fallback; the Web UI sign-in above is recommended.

# Sign in to the China site (the default; equivalent to --site cn)
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-workbuddy-login

# Sign in to the international site
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-workbuddy-login --site intl

# Show the signed-in account, its site, and the model list
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-workbuddy-login --status

# Remove the stored credential
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-workbuddy-login --logout
```

Once signed in, WorkBuddy's models appear in the model picker.

## Build

From a source checkout:

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run build
```

This compiles the host half with `tsc` and bundles the Web client half with `esbuild`, both into `lib/`.

## Provenance and license

MIT. This plugin is a WorkBuddy adaptation of
[`@shatyuka/dsh-llm-codebuddy`](https://github.com/shatyuka/dsh-llm-codebuddy)
(MIT, © 2026 Shatyuka), which is the original work it derives from: the host
architecture, the browser-OAuth handshake, the model-catalog reader, the
settings page, and the usage indicator are all its author's design. This
repository re-points that client at the WorkBuddy deployments — the site list,
the product token every request identifies itself as, and the provider,
settings, and credential identifiers are WorkBuddy's — and renames it
accordingly. The upstream copyright notice is retained in
[`LICENSE`](./LICENSE) as the license requires.

When the upstream project releases fixes, they can be diffed in against this
tree: the changes here are confined to the identifiers, the two service roots
in `src/constants.ts`, and the catalogue User-Agent documented there.

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin: ask_user_question popup enhancement - selecting an option reveals a per-option note input, sent to the model with the selection
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-question-note

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-question-note.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-question-note)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-question-note.svg)](LICENSE)

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）「交互式问答」弹窗增强插件：**用户点选某个选项后，在该选项正下方出现一个可选的补充说明输入框；填写的内容与选中的选项一并传给模型。**

## 效果

- 原版弹窗的样式、功能、交互全部保留（组件是官方 `QuestionComposer` 的忠实移植，同一套 CSS 令牌与几何）。
- **补充说明按选项独立存储**：每个被选中的选项下方各有一个自己的补充输入框，互不共享、不随勾选变化移动；取消勾选时输入框隐藏，文字保留（重新勾选会恢复）。单选题换选选项时同理，各选项各记各的。
- 提交时答案格式不变：`{ "answers": [ { "id": "...", "selected": ["选项文字"], "custom": "…" } ] }`。`custom` 的组装规则：单选 = 补充文本原文；多选 = 每个有补充的选项一行、格式「选项文字: 补充」（模型可分清哪句对应哪个选项）；底部自由回答行若有内容追加在最后。不填补充说明时行为与原版完全一致。
- 底部「其他（自定义输入）」行保留，是独立的自由回答入口（单选打字清空已选 = 原版语义；多选与勾选并存 = 原版语义）。
- 计划审查（plan-review）类卡片、审批卡片、超时后续答、已结算回答回看等全部由官方组件处理，本插件不接管。

## 与原版的唯一行为差异

启用后，**单选点选项不再自动跳到下一题**（原版会跳，但那会让用户没机会填写补充说明），而是停留在当前题并展开输入框；在输入框里回车或点「下一题」按钮进入下一题，最后一题回车即提交。

## 实现原理（面向二次开发者）

- 纯客户端 Cordis 插件：浏览器半往 `conversation.composer` 链式槽以 `priority: -10`（官方在默认 0）注册增强版组件，链选举「数值小者先跑、第一个 select 非 null 者胜出」，因此增强版先被询问并接管通用问题卡的渲染；官方插件的卡片注册、倒计时、投影、续答机制原样复用（`src/client/carrier.ts` 以结构化方式消费官方载体对象）。
- 鸭子类型失配时 `select` 返回 null → 安全降级为官方弹窗（功能缺失但弹窗可用）。
- 合并方案零协议改动：宿主端 `userQuestions.answer()` 只校验「每题恰好回答一次」，不禁止 `selected` 与 `custom` 并存；工具结果与超时续答消息都是原样 JSON 透传。

## 开发与安装

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm run build     # 产出 lib/index.js（宿主半）与 lib/client.js（浏览器半）
pnpm run check     # 产物语法检查

# 安装到 desktop 配置（会写入 dsh.profile.bundles，需重启 DSH 生效）
dsh plugin --profile desktop add <本目录路径或 npm 包名>
```

## 版本兼容

针对 DSH 0.2.0-rc 族（`@deepseek-ai/*` peer `^0.2.0-rc.1`）。官方弹窗组件内部结构若在后续版本变化，需同步调整 `src/client/carrier.ts` 的结构匹配与 `src/client/composer.tsx` 的移植。

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: a 5px dot left of the model name in the composer tool row — yellow for DeepSeek peak hours, green for off-peak (half price). Rendered only when the session's model provider is DeepSeek.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator

**See the current DeepSeek API pricing window at a glance in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) Web GUI.**

A single 5px dot sits in the composer tool row, **just left of the model name** (**rendered only when the
session's selected model provider is DeepSeek**):

| Color | Window | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🟡 Yellow `#f2b705` | Peak hours | Standard |
| 🟢 Green `#22c55e` | Off-peak hours | Half price |

Nothing else is rendered — no text, no icon, no placeholder copy (the dot carries an
`aria-label` for screen readers). No build step, no third-party dependencies: the whole
plugin is one file.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

## When it shows

The dot renders only while the session's selected model provider is DeepSeek; otherwise it
renders nothing at all and takes no space:

| Provider | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `deepseek-official` (DeepSeek API key) | ✅ |
| `deepseek-account` (DeepSeek account) | ✅ |
| Anything else (Anthropic, an OpenAI-compatible gateway, a self-hosted proxy, …) | ❌ hidden |
| Unknown (model directory still loading) | ❌ hidden |

The provider is what counts, not the model name — a third-party gateway serving a DeepSeek
model does not get DeepSeek's time-of-day pricing. The rule lives in `isDeepSeekProvider()`;
change that one function to change the policy.

The session's model directory is resolved **after mount, with retries**: a freshly switched
session has not registered its scope yet, so the lookup legitimately fails for a moment. The
dot therefore appears a fraction of a second after a session switch instead of staying hidden
for the whole session.

## How the window is decided

Per DeepSeek's official pricing page
([Models & Pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing)):

- **Peak**: Beijing time **Monday–Friday** (excluding Chinese statutory holidays),
  **09:00–12:00** and **14:00–18:00**;
- **Off-peak**: everything else, **including weekends and statutory holidays all day**
  (off-peak = half of the peak price).

Intervals are half-open: 12:00 and 18:00 sharp already count as off-peak, while 09:00 and
14:00 sharp count as peak. All comparisons use `Asia/Shanghai`, so the machine's own time
zone does not matter.

> **Make-up workdays.** The official wording is "Monday to Friday … all other periods,
> including weekends and Chinese statutory holidays, are off-peak all day". A Saturday or
> Sunday that the government designates as a make-up workday therefore stays off-peak
> (green) here. Change the `WORKDAYS` check in `client.js` if you disagree.

## Installation

Requires a working DSH profile (desktop app or `dsh web`).

The recommended way is to **paste a GitHub address into the Plugins page** — no clone and no
commands:

1. Open the **Plugins** page from the sidebar (the plugin icon in the panel list).
2. Click **Add plugin**.
3. Paste this address into the field (it accepts a package name, a GitHub repository address,
   or a local directory path):

   ```
   https://github.com/cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
   ```

   The shorthand `github:cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator` works too; add a branch or
   commit to pin a revision, e.g.
   `github:cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator#<commit-sha>`.

4. It is live as soon as it finishes: the result reads `application: applied` and the open
   page needs no refresh. If it reports `restart-required`, restart Harness.

The installer writes the package into the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` and dependencies,
and inserts the loader row declared by this repository's own `cordis.patch.yml` — you never
edit a config file by hand.

### Installing through the agent (equivalent)

```
plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=github:cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
```

Before installing, the manager runs a `git ls-remote` reachability check against the
repository (public repos need no credentials).

### Installing from a local directory (when editing the code)

1. Clone the repository:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator.git
   ```

2. Paste the **absolute path** of the clone into the same field (or hand it to the agent):

   ```
   plugin_manager  action=install_bundle  target=/absolute/path/to/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
   ```

   The profile records a `link:` dependency, so re-installing after an edit is enough.

**Update**: re-installing the **same source** does **not** take effect — the dependency is
unchanged, so the installer reports `ambiguous-install`. Uninstall on the Plugins page first,
then add the same address again:

```
plugin_manager  action=remove_bundle  target=dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
plugin_manager  action=install_bundle target=github:cumthugo/dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator
```

The host re-reads the bundle and pushes it to the open page, so no restart is needed. (The
local-directory flavour works the same way — swap the second target for the clone path;
switching to a different source, e.g. from a local path to the GitHub address, also avoids
the ambiguity.)
**Disable / uninstall**: toggle the row on the GUI Plugins page, or use `plugin_manager`'s
`remove_bundle` with the package name `dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator`.

> The package name matches the repository (`dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator`) and is not
> published to npm — install it by local path or from GitHub as shown above. The name must
> match the `id` in `client.js`'s `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id })` and the entry `name`
> in `cordis.patch.yml`: change one and all three must change, followed by a reinstall.

## Holiday data and automatic refresh

Holidays are only used to exclude statutory days off from the peak windows. Three sources,
in priority order:

1. **Local cache** — `localStorage` key `dsh-deepseek-offpeak-indicator:holidays:<year>`, considered
   fresh for 30 days;
2. **Network refresh** — the year JSON from
   [holiday-cn](https://github.com/NateScarlet/holiday-cn) (which scrapes the State Council
   holiday notices), trying `raw.githubusercontent.com` then `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, with a 6 s
   timeout;
3. **Built-in fallback** — `BUILTIN_HOLIDAYS` in `client.js` (currently 2026, 33 days off).

So **next year's schedule takes effect automatically once published**, with no code change,
provided the machine can reach one of those two hosts. Fully offline, the built-in table is
used; for a year with neither cache nor built-in data the plugin degrades to a
weekend-only rule (that year's holidays would be misread as peak during 09:00–12:00 and
14:00–18:00).

To refresh the built-in table offline:

```bash
node tools/update-holidays.mjs            # existing years + this year and the next
node tools/update-holidays.mjs 2027       # only the given years
```

Run the remove → install flow above afterwards, so the page picks up the new built-in table.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | Bundle manifest: `dsh.bundle.patch` and the `dsh.client` declaration |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Inserts the `deepseek-offpeak-indicator` loader row |
| `index.js` | Host half, empty `apply()` (it exists so the loader has a host row) |
| `client.js` | Browser half: window logic, the dot component, slot registration (one file, no build) |
| `tools/update-holidays.mjs` | Regenerates the built-in holiday table |
| `tools/test-classify.mjs` | Regression tests: peak windows, the provider gate, and the session-switch resolve/retry path (31 assertions) |

## Customizing

Everything lives at the top of `client.js`: `PEAK_WINDOWS`, `PEAK_COLOR` /
`OFFPEAK_COLOR`, `DOT_SIZE` (default `5`), `DEEPSEEK_PROVIDER_IDS` /
`isDeepSeekProvider()` (which providers count as DeepSeek), plus the slot and its placement —
the dot registers into `conversation.input.right`, which renders immediately left of the model
name, and `nudgeX` / `nudgeY` shift it by a few pixels (currently `16` / `1`). To move it
elsewhere change `name` in `ctx.slots.register` (e.g. `conversation.input.left`,
`conversation.composer.dock`) and adjust `id` accordingly.

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://github.com/ymck-x/dsh-skill-starter/archive/refs/tags/v0.3.0.tar.gz
```

`desktop` 换成你自己的 profile 名（`~/.dsh/profiles/` 下面的目录名）。装完重启 `dsh`。

> **请照抄这个完整地址，不要改成 `refs/heads/main.tar.gz`。**
> 分支地址的内容会随作者推代码而改变，而 pnpm 会记下你安装当时的指纹。
> 之后你装**任何**插件时，pnpm 都会重新核对全部旧依赖，一旦发现指纹对不上就中止整次安装
> （`ERR_PNPM_TARBALL_INTEGRITY`），而且报错指向一个你当时根本没在装的包。
> `refs/tags/` 指向一次固定发布，内容永不改变。

也不要写成 `github:ymck-x/dsh-skill-starter` 这种简写：它会被 pnpm 解析成 SSH 地址（`git+ssh://`），而匿名 SSH 访问 GitHub 会被直接拒绝，装不上。

验证：设置页里出现「**Skill 管理**」这一项，或者直接问 AI「我有哪些技能」。

### 没有 dsh 命令时手动装

`dsh plugin add` 内部就是「pnpm 装包 + 把包名写进 `dsh.profile.bundles`」。你也可以自己做这两步：

```sh
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop
pnpm add https://github.com/ymck-x/dsh-skill-starter/archive/refs/tags/v0.3.0.tar.gz
```

再把 `dsh-skill-starter` 加进同一个目录里 `package.json` 的 `dsh.profile.bundles`：

```json
{
  "dsh": {
    "profile": {
      "bundles": [
        "@deepseek-ai/dsh-base",
        "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app",
        "dsh-skill-starter"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

重启 `dsh` 即生效。

### 卸载

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-skill-starter
```

手动装的：从 `bundles` 里删掉这一项，再 `pnpm remove dsh-skill-starter`。

**卸载不影响你写的技能**——它们在 `~\.dsh\skills\` 里，不属于插件。

## 它做什么

### 一、设置页里的面板

打开「设置 → Skill 管理」，你看到的是**按你遇到的问题分的组**，不是按名字排的字母序：

```
开工之前
  先把票据和规格放在哪定下来。
  setup-tickets

别让它做错方向
  动手之前，把没问清的问完。
  ask-first

看不懂就拉回来
  说「没看懂」时，用大白话重讲上一段。
  plain-words

别让「改好了」是空话
  先说清用什么办法验证，改完真的跑一遍再报告。
  prove-it
  一次只走一小步，每步验证过再继续。
  tiny-steps

让它记住你的做法
  一句话把你的做法记成技能文件。
  write-my-skill
```

选一条就能改：名称、描述、使用时机、正文，还有两个调用开关。也能新建、删除、把内置技能复制一份出来改。中英双语，跟着界面语言走。

### 二、「我该用哪个」

面板里有一块处境对照表，直接显示路由技能里那张表——现在 29 行，点一行就跳到对应的技能。

这张表**不是复制过来的**：插件每次从 `skills-map/SKILL.md` 现读现解析，所以它和路由技能永远是同一份内容，不会两边说法不一致。

### 三、技能包

技能包是「一组相关技能，一次装完」。自带一个：

| 包 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `engineering-zh` | 20 个中文工程流程技能：拷问需求 → 收成规格 → 拆票 → 实现 → 双轴审查 → 复盘，外加诊断 bug、TDD、原型、研究、教学、交接 |

**升级不覆盖你的修改**，三层保护：

| 情况 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 你改过这个文件 | 跳过，并在结果里点名 |
| 文件已存在且内容不同 | **绝不覆盖**，单独列出 |
| 内容相同 | 只登记指纹，不动文件 |

所以想改包里的技能，直接改用户目录里那份就行，不用担心下次升级被冲掉。

### 四、模型能直接用

插件注册六个工具，AI 在对话里就能读写技能库、装卸技能包，不用你打开设置页：

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `skill_list` | 列出全部技能：来源、调用方式、是否被覆盖、附件数 |
| `skill_read` | 读出完整内容与附件清单 |
| `skill_write` | 新建或修改 |
| `skill_delete` | 删除 |
| `skill_pack_list` | 技能包状态 |
| `skill_pack_install` | 安装或升级，不覆盖你的改动 |

所以你说「把这套流程记下来」，它会直接落盘，不会写错格式。

## 为什么这么设计

### 问题一：技能写完了没人用

技能要生效，得有人知道它什么时候该上场。三种做法叠起来解决：

- **描述里写用户的原话**。`tdd` 的描述是「说『写个测试再实现』『先红后绿』时使用」——AI 靠这句判断该不该自己调用。
- **面板按症状分组**。用户先看到症状（「别让『改好了』是空话」），再看到药。
- **只给人用的技能明确标出来**。会改变工作状态的动作（收规格、拆票、交接、复盘）只允许你手动发起，AI 不能自己决定。

### 问题二：装了一堆，不知道什么时候用哪个

二十多个技能，靠记名字不现实。所以有一张按**处境**写的对照表：

| 你现在的处境 | 加载哪个技能 |
|---|---|
| 有个想法，要把它问清楚 | `grilling` |
| 需求没说清，要先把该问的一次问完 | `ask-first` |
| 要在一个项目里建好票据约定 | `setup-tickets` |
| 要把已经聊清楚的结论写成规格 | `to-spec` |
| 要把规格拆成多张票据 | `to-tickets` |
| 做完了，不知道改动有没有问题 | `code-review` |
| 没坏，但比以前慢很多 | `diagnosing-bugs` |
| 这段代码改一次要动好几个地方 | `improve-codebase-architecture` |
| 不确定这个模块该怎么切 | `codebase-design` |
| 同一个词团队里有两个意思 | `domain-modeling` |
| 答案在别人脑子里 | `to-questionnaire` |
| 没听懂上一条 | `wait-what` |

完整 29 行在面板里，也在 `skills-map` 技能里。

### 问题三：技能越多，每轮对话越贵

技能的描述是**常驻**的——不管用不用，它都在每轮请求里占位置。所以插件把这个成本算清楚并公布：

| 部分 | 规模 | 估算 |
|---|---|---|
| 插件自带 6 个技能 | 448 字 | 约 269 到 538 token |
| 技能包 20 个技能（装了才有） | 1776 字 | 约 1066 到 2131 token |
| 六个工具的 schema | 671 字 | 约 403 到 805 token |
| **设置面板** | — | **0**（只在浏览器里跑） |
| **合计（装了技能包）** | 2895 字 | **约 1737 到 3474 token** |

不想要工具那部分开销，可以在配置里关掉：

```yaml
- id: dsh-skill-starter
  config:
    enableTools: false
```

关掉之后模型侧开销归零，设置面板照常。「我该用哪个」那块表也照常——它走面板自己的接口，不进模型上下文。

自己量一遍：

```sh
node measure.mjs
```

### 问题四：升级把改动覆盖了

上面那三层保护就是答案。设计上是这么想的：**技能包给的是起点，不是终点**。装进来之后那份文件归你，插件只负责以后添新技能、修错别字，不碰你动过的任何一行。

## 技能清单

技能分两类，区别在**谁能调用**：

- **模型可调用**：任务合适时 AI 会自己用；你也能打 `/名字` 手动调。
- **只允许人工发起**：只有你打出 `/名字` 才生效。它们会改变工作状态，不该由 AI 自己决定什么时候做。

### 插件自带（6 个基础技能）

| 技能 | 什么时候用 |
|---|---|
| `ask-first` | 用户提出还没说清的需求（「加个导出功能」） |

| `write-my-skill` | 用户说「把这条记下来」「以后都这样做」 |
| `setup-tickets` | 要给一个项目建票据约定 |

**只允许人工发起（9 个）**

| 技能 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `to-spec` | 把已经聊定的结论收成一份规格 |
| `to-tickets` | 拆成一组能各自收工的票据 |
| `implement` | 按票据逐张做出来 |
| `retro` | 回看这段会话，改进工作环境 |
| `handoff` | 压成交接文档，换人换机器接着干 |
| `to-questionnaire` | 答案在别人手里时，写一份问卷去问 |
| `wait-what` | 没听懂上一条，用大白话重讲 |
| `teach` | 跨多次会话学一门东西 |
| `improve-codebase-architecture` | 扫出结构改进机会，给候选让你挑 |

**模型可调用（11 个）**

| 技能 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `grilling` | 把还没想清的想法问到没有含糊 |
| `skills-map` | 路由表：从处境查到该用哪个 |
| `tdd` | 测试先行的红-绿循环 |
| `diagnosing-bugs` | 疑难 bug 的诊断纪律 |
| `code-review` | 双轴审查：规范轴 + 规格轴 |

技能包里的正文保持一屏内；词汇表、判断标准、例证这类细节放在同目录的附件里，正文末尾有一行指针。`tdd` 带 `MOCKING.md`，`code-review` 带 `SMELLS.md`，`codebase-design` 带 `DEEP-MODULES.md`，一共 10 份附件。

## 技能的三种来源

| 来源 | 位置 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 项目级 | `<项目>\.dsh\skills\`、`<项目>\.agents\skills\` | 跟着仓库走，DSH 原生扫描 |
| 用户级 | `~\.dsh\skills\` | 面板和工具都管这里 |
| 内置 | 插件自带的 `skills\` | 只读；在用户目录放一份同名的就能覆盖 |

**同名时优先级：项目级 > 用户级 > 内置。** 项目根按「最近的含 `.git` 的目录」判定，所以在子目录里也能找到。

面板只列用户级和内置（浏览器端拿不到会话的工作目录）；项目级技能在对话里问 AI 就能看到。

## 和同类插件的关系

DSH 生态里已经有两个做技能的插件，侧重和我们不同：

| 插件 | 侧重 |
|---|---|
| `dsh-skills` | 把散落各处（Claude Code、项目目录、`.skill` 包）的技能**汇总入库**，引用或副本两种方式，能导出打包 |
| `asakumizy/dsh-local-skills` | 本地技能浏览器，Notion 风格的界面 |
| **本插件** | **技能内容本身 + 分发**：自带一整套能用的技能，用技能包分发，管升级与本地改动 |

三个装在一起不冲突（id 不同），只是功能有重叠。**同一个技能名不要装两份**，那样每个技能会被注册两次。

## 开发

```sh
node verify.mjs        # 自测 59 项：解析、增删改查、路径安全、工具定义、技能包、项目级扫描、路由表
node check-tools.mjs   # 用 DSH 自己的 JSON Schema 校验器检查六个工具的定义
node check-pack.mjs    # 检查技能包内容是否符合规范
node measure.mjs       # 量出每轮对话的固定开销
```

**技能文件**（`skills/*/SKILL.md`）改动会热生效，保存即用。

**插件代码**（`index.js`、`client.js`）改动需要重载：`client.js` 刷新页面即可；`index.js` 因为 Node 会缓存已加载的模块，要把插件卸掉再装（或重启 DSH）。

要往包里加技能、或者重写技能时，先读 [`REWRITE-GUIDE.md`](REWRITE-GUIDE.md)：那里记了附件该怎么分类（模板类压进正文，方法类与机制类必须留附件），以及第一次重写时因为「一律单文件」而丢掉 19% 内容的教训。

### 目录结构

```
dsh-skill-starter/
  package.json           插件清单（dsh.bundle.patch 指向下面的补丁）
  cordis.patch.yml       告诉 DSH 加载这个插件
  index.js               宿主侧：注册内置技能、六个工具，提供面板接口
  client.js              浏览器侧：设置页「Skill 管理」面板
  skills/                6 个基础技能
  packs/engineering-zh/  技能包：20 个技能 + 10 份附件
  verify.mjs             自测
  check-tools.mjs        工具定义校验
  check-pack.mjs         技能包规范校验
  measure.mjs            成本测量
  REWRITE-GUIDE.md       重写或新增技能的规范
  CHANGELOG.md           更新记录
```

---

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: Unofficial DSH TUI plugin for Orca terminal readiness and finalized completion
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Orca Terminal Status

An unofficial, independent DeepSeek Harness plugin that reports real DSH TUI
readiness and completion to Orca's existing terminal status channel. MIT licensed.
No modified Orca application is required.

## Why

With Orca 1.4.220, DSH can finish a request while Orca still waits for `tui-idle`:
DSH's Claude-compatible hooks report HTTP events, whereas that readiness check
expects terminal status. See [Orca issue #25257](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/issues/25257)
and [the upstream PR](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/26074).

This plugin listens directly to DSH lifecycle events; it does not translate an
HTTP `Stop` into completion. `Stop` can still enqueue continuation work.

- Reports startup readiness only after the TUI's actual child runtime finishes
  activation and the single root agent is idle with an empty inbox.
- Reports `working` for a running root and `done` for finalized idle, using
  ordered OSC 9999 writes to the existing PTY.
- Ignores subagents, ambiguous multiple roots, non-TTY SDK output, and terminals
  without Orca's pane environment. Requires matching frontend/service ownership.
- Leaves Orca's existing HTTP hooks in place for their existing purposes.

## Tested versions

| Component | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Official Orca | 1.4.220 |
| Official DSH / dsh-agent | 0.2.0-rc.2 |
| Community `@deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui` | 0.13.0 |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis` | 4.0.4 |
| `@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader` | 1.0.5 |
| Real integration platform | macOS, Apple Silicon |

This implementation depends on TUI/Cordis internals (`internal/status`, fiber
state/parent/store and `dsh-tui-runtime`), in addition to DSH's plugin loader.
Plugin-loader compatibility alone does not guarantee those internals remain
compatible. The manifest declares the tested peer versions; optional peers avoid
automatically installing another DSH or TUI copy. Missing TUI does not provide
readiness. Revalidate upgrades; compatibility with other versions, Windows,
Linux, SSH and multi-root frontend routing has not been established.

## Install

Use Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24` and an existing DSH TUI profile. Install exactly
once: do not combine this bundle with a manually inserted copy of the plugin or
an Orca release that already emits the same DSH PTY status. Installing a bundle
changes every session using that profile; schedule installation between sessions.

Through DSH's official package-management CLI (replace `dsh-tui` with your profile):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add https://github.com/Alex-wangyang/dsh-orca-terminal-status/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-orca-terminal-status-0.1.0.tgz
```

Alternatively, download and extract that release, then ask DSH's native
`plugin_manager` to use `action: install_bundle` with `target` set to the absolute
extracted package directory. This package contains `dsh.bundle.patch`, no runtime
dependencies, no build step and no install/prepare scripts. npm registry publication
is not required. Do not run `npm install` inside DSH's profile yourself.

Restart DSH after package replacement and launch it inside Orca. Verify the
composed plugin row and native `tui-idle` readiness, then run a harmless task and
verify completion. A saved bundle selection alone does not prove runtime health.

Remove the bundle using the same profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui remove dsh-orca-terminal-status
```

This removes the bundle-managed plugin, not an older manually installed home
patch. Preserve Orca-managed hook rows when removing a manual installation.

## Verification

```sh
npm test
npm pack --dry-run
```

Eight behavioral tests cover delayed/failed frontend activation, root and inbox
guards, child events, Stop continuations, ordered immediate wake, SDK isolation,
disposal and frontend ownership. They need no model credentials or DSH installation.

The same runtime source was exercised against the tested real stack: cold worker
launch and same-process worker reuse both admitted successfully, wrote independently
verified task marker files, and reported native worker completion. Orca's native
`tui-idle` check also passed after completion and on a fresh final-source launch.
The official Orca application bytes were unchanged. These are bounded integration
results, not a guarantee for later releases. Release packaging is separately tested
with DSH's native installer in an isolated profile.

## 中文

这是独立维护的非官方插件。它监听 DSH 的真实状态，把就绪、工作中和完成状态
写入 Orca 已有的终端通路，使官方 Orca 也能正确识别 DSH worker。
它不会把 HTTP `Stop` 直接当作任务完成，也不需要修改 Orca 本体。

安装命令见上方；`dsh-tui` 应替换为实际使用的 profile。请勿重复安装手工副本
和 bundle。已实测的版本组合见表格；插件加载机制保持兼容，并不代表 TUI
内部生命周期永远保持兼容，因此 DSH/TUI 升级后仍需验证。

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). Independently maintained; not affiliated with or endorsed by
DeepSeek AI, the DSH TUI maintainers, or Stably/Orca.

# DSH Chinese Minimal Custom Mode English | [中文](README.zh.md) Retains the complete `dsh-custom-mode` Settings UI for editing the system prompt, switching the base mode, toggling plugin rows, and managing multiple assistants. This fork changes only the first-install defaults: Minimal base mode and the complete system prompt `你是一个中文助手`.

## Install Install the stable GemChance GitHub release: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/GemChance/dsh-chinese-minimal-mode/tar.gz/refs/tags/v2.3.0 ``` Restart the process that serves the profile. The version on the settings page is the one that is running. Desktop app: install from the in-app Plugins page. The CLI cannot modify `profiles/desktop`. On Windows, `install.sh` is bash and it needs a `dsh` executable on `PATH`. Otherwise use the `dsh` shipped with DeepSeek Harness, or `node node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js`. ## Use 1. Open Settings → Custom mode. 2. Edit the system prompt. Save is directly under the editor. 3. A new session uses this assistant when `settings.yaml` has no `agent-presets.default` yet. An existing value is left as it is. On first install, the plugin creates Custom mode with the Minimal base and initializes `prompt.md` to `你是一个中文助手`. Everything remains editable from Settings, and upgrades do not overwrite existing user data. The prompt is `prompt.md`. The next time a model step is assembled, that file is read again. History can load an older draft into the editor; loading does not write. A save computed against an older copy is refused when the file changed underneath. The model can change the same file only through `custom_prompt`, which asks first. The page is two branches. This assistant edits the one you have open, and all five base modes can be chosen. New assistant writes only when you click New assistant: Coding, Writing, and Chat stay selectable, and only the official Standard mode is lit. The other four official modes are dim and cannot be chosen there. | Posture | After create | | --- | --- | | Develop | Official Standard mode, tools as shipped. | | Write | Official Standard mode. Terminal off, file tools on. | | Chat | Official Standard mode. Files and terminal off. | ## Boundaries - It does not replace Standard, PTC, Minimal, or Creator. - It does not ship a role-play preset. - It does not run in the desktop profile from the CLI. Headless mode will not start a session that uses an agent preset. ## Compatibility Declared range: `>=0.1.5-rc.2 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.1.6-alpha.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.1.7-alpha.1 <0.2.0-0 || >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0 || >=0.2.1-alpha.1 <0.3.0-0` | dsh | Claim | Checked for 2.3.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | `0.2.0-rc.2` | declared | Windows web profile, before this release | | `0.2.1-alpha.1` | declared, in CI | not re-run for this release | | `0.1.7-rc.2` | declared, in CI | not re-run for this release | The unit suite also passed under WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04 (Node only, no dsh process, no browser). That is not a Linux desktop result. ## Docs - [docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) — wrong version installed, base mode unavailable, half-finished upgrade - [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) — where the prompt is read, and which host calls this package depends on - [docs/PUBLISHING.md](docs/PUBLISHING.md) — tags and release - [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — people - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — agents ## License MIT

plugins.description: Connect DeepSeek Harness to a ChatGPT subscription through official browser sign-in. macOS community add-on.
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH OpenAI subscription add-on

![Installation guide: install the add-on, connect your ChatGPT plan, and choose a model in DSH](docs/installation.gif)

Install this small add-on after installing ordinary DeepSeek Harness. It adds OpenAI models and reasoning controls to DSH, using the official Sign in with ChatGPT subscription flow.

## Connect

This first release supports **macOS**, Node.js 22+, macOS Command Line Tools, pnpm, and **DSH 0.2.1-alpha.1**. It does not bundle another DSH runtime.

If DSH is not installed yet:

```sh
npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.1 pnpm
```

Install the shared package, then connect:

```sh
npm install -g pnpm https://github.com/teilomillet/dsh-openai-subscription/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-openai-subscription-0.1.0.tgz
```
```sh
dsh-openai connect
```
```sh
dsh web
```

The connection command installs the provider into DSH's existing **web** profile and opens official browser sign-in. Allow the app to use your ChatGPT plan. In DSH, select a workspace, open the model menu, and choose **OpenAI subscription (ChatGPT)**. The **Effort** submenu exposes the documented options for that model. Restart DSH after connecting if it was already running.

Your other DSH providers, model selection, tools, and sessions remain intact. Usage counts against your ChatGPT plan. This add-on uses text and function tools; image input and native OpenAI hosted tools are not implemented.

The account model list can omit GPT-6.1 Sol. Connection makes at most one 60-second low-effort check for an omitted, previously unverified GPT-6.1 Sol, and adds it locally only after completed inference. That check uses a small amount of your plan allowance. Other reasoning levels come from official model capability documentation. Failed verification leaves the discovered models available. Reconnecting a verified profile avoids another access check.

## Share or install through Git

Share the **.tgz file**, or commit this package's source with its .gitignore. No login credentials or account-specific model state belong in the repository.

To build a package from source:

```sh
npm ci
npm pack
```

The pack step builds the vendored SDK automatically. Send the generated tarball to the other computer and run the connection commands there. Each person signs in with their own account.

## Commands

```sh
dsh-openai connect                 # install web provider and sign in
dsh-openai connect --profile headless
dsh-openai login                   # reconnect without reinstalling
dsh-openai status
dsh-openai models
dsh-openai logout
```

Without a global add-on installation, DSH's native plugin commands work too:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-openai-subscription-0.1.0.tgz
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-openai login
dsh web
```

To remove the provider from a profile, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-openai-subscription`. Run logout first if you also want to disconnect the subscription.

## Local state and security

Authentication, model discovery, and the Keychain helper are stored under `$DSH_HOME/openai-subscription/` (normally `~/.dsh/openai-subscription/`). `DSH_OPENAI_HOME` can select a separate state directory. OAuth state is encrypted with a key stored in macOS Keychain; credentials are not copied from Codex. The package and generated tarball exclude all account state, sessions, model overrides, caches, and installed dependencies. Browser consent remains an explicit user action.

Windows and Linux are not supported by this release. The macOS helper needs Command Line Tools to compile on first use; install them using `xcode-select --install` if needed.

## License and provenance

This package and its modified Sign in with ChatGPT DevKit are distributed under the included **Sign-in with ChatGPT DevKit Noncommercial License**. Personal noncommercial experimentation is allowed; commercial use is outside this license. Vendor licenses, third-party notices, source, and modification notices are included. This is a community add-on, not an official DeepSeek or OpenAI product.

Inspected source revisions: Harness 5badb15009ae1756c3afe0ae0cef1faafc290ccc; DevKit f723814abdccec135b519c451fb6e1992ee5e933.

- [Official subscription sign-in](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/quickstart)
- [Models and inference](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference)
- [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

plugins.description: Push DeepSeek Harness agent notifications to your phone and watch via ntfy, Bark, Gotify, Telegram or a webhook.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-notify-push
Push DeepSeek Harness agent notifications to your phone and watch via ntfy, Bark, Gotify, Telegram or a webhook — without keeping the browser tab open.
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/icrefin/dsh-notify-push?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/icrefin/dsh-notify-push?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/releases/tag/v0.4.1)
[![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/icrefin/dsh-notify-push?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/commits/main)
[![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/icrefin/dsh-notify-push?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/stargazers)
[![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/icrefin/dsh-notify-push/pulls)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.17-339933?style=flat-square&logo=node.js)](https://nodejs.org)
[![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-0.2.0--rc.2-4B5563?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh)
plugin. It pushes a short notification to your **phone** — and, through the
phone's own notification mirroring, to your **watch** — whenever an agent
finishes a turn, hits an error, or is waiting on your approval.

Unlike a browser notification, this leaves the machine: it goes out over the
network to a push service you choose, so it arrives while the Harness tab is
closed and the laptop lid is shut.

```
Settings ▸ Notify Push                          v0.4.1
└── delivery state, an editable configuration form,
    the exact server and topic to subscribe to, armed triggers,
    a live preview, the delivery log,
    and one "Send test notification" button
```

It is a section of the Settings panel, not a page in the working area: a
notifier is configured once and glanced at occasionally, so giving it a permanent
sidebar icon and a whole centre column overstated it. The Settings shell owns the
trigger, the nav entry, the panel and the scrolling container, so this plugin
contributes only the section body — deliberately with no `height`, no second
scroll and no horizontal padding, all of which the shell already provides.

The version beside the title is read from the manifest **at runtime**, not baked
in at build time, so it names the build the harness actually loaded. That matters
because installing a new package does not re-compose a running profile: a swap on
disk leaves the old code live until a restart, and the chip is the fastest way to
tell those two situations apart.

## What a notification says

Every notification carries the same three facts, in a fixed shape:

| Part | Where | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **event type** | title | `Agent finished` |
| **host** | title | `workstation.local` |
| **session** | body line 1 | `Fix the login redirect` |
| **detail** | body line 2 | `done in 42s` |

So a lock screen reads:

```
Agent finished · workstation.local
Fix the login redirect
done in 42s
```

The event type is one of `Agent finished`, `Agent error`, `Approval needed`,
`Question asked` or `Test notification`. `titlePrefix` prepends a literal
(`DSH · …`) when you run more than one Harness.

A `Question asked` notification carries the question itself, not just word that
one exists — a prompt that only said "the agent has a question" would make you
open the app to find out whether it mattered:

```
Question asked · workstation.local
Fix the login redirect
Choose Mode — Which deployment should I target?
Blue · Green
```

The heading, the question and (when there are a few) the offered choices, so the
lock screen carries enough to decide whether to answer now. A longer question is
truncated here, with a visible ellipsis, rather than left for the OS to cut
mid-word.

## Screenshots

![Notification pipeline](docs/images/notification-flow.png)
*How an event reaches your phone: the engine paces and de-duplicates, the formatter composes the two lines, the provider delivers.*

![Notification preview](docs/images/notification-preview.png)
*Rendered from this plugin's own formatter output — the exact title and body strings, shown as they appear on a lock screen. Not a device screenshot.*

![Settings section layout](docs/images/settings-section-mockup.png)
*Layout mockup of the **Settings ▸ Notify Push** section (illustrative, not a screenshot).*

## Surfaces

| Surface | What it does |
|---|---|
| Host route `GET /api/dsh-notify-push/status` | provider, destination, armed triggers, counters, live preview, form descriptors |
| Host route `GET /api/dsh-notify-push/history` | the recent delivery log |
| Host route `POST /api/dsh-notify-push/test` | send one synthetic notification |
| Host route `POST /api/dsh-notify-push/config` | merge validated settings into this row's config |
| Settings section **Notify Push** | the whole surface: status, form, subscribe block, preview, log and test button |

One slot registration, into `settings.section` — a `list` slot declared by
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-general`, whose entries carry
`{ id, order, label }` and whose active entry the shell renders inside its own
scrolling panel. `dsh.client.inject` names both that package and
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings`, which owns the canonical slot contract and
is what makes the registration type-check against the real slot map.

Every route is loopback-fenced, method-checked and body-size-capped. The config
route additionally validates its patch against the field specs before anything is
written — a rejected key never reaches the settings document, which outlives the
process and would otherwise be reapplied on every boot.

## Install

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm check                              # typecheck both halves, build, then vitest
pnpm run pack                           # -> dist/dsh-notify-push-0.4.1.tgz
```

The desktop profile is owned by the Electron application, so `dsh plugin add`
refuses it: install the packed tarball from **Settings → Plugins**. A bundle
added to a running profile needs a **restart** before its entry can be imported;
the browser half additionally needs the page reloaded.

## Configure

**Edit it in the panel.** Open **Settings → Notify Push**; the **Configuration**
section renders a form for the selected provider: pick the backend, fill in its
fields, press Save. A saved value applies **immediately** — no restart — because
every field of the row's schema is `volatile`, so the loader swaps it into the
running fiber rather than waiting for the next boot. It is also written to the
host's settings document, so it comes back after a restart.

Secret fields (tokens, device keys) are **write-only**: the stored value never
leaves the host, so the input starts blank and shows `stored` or `not set`.
Leaving it blank keeps what is there — there is no clear action, deliberately, so
a save can never wipe a working credential by accident.

Each secret field carries its own eye button, which unmasks **what you are
typing** so you can check a paste before saving. It cannot show the stored value,
because the browser was never given it — an untouched field stays empty with its
`stored` placeholder, revealed or not.

Configuration also works from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, which survives
plugin upgrades. The row id is `dsh-notify-push`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-notify-push
  name: dsh-notify-push
  config:
    provider: ntfy
    ntfyServer: https://ntfy.sh
    ntfyTopic: <a long random topic>
```

Both paths write the same thing, so you can set a value in YAML and later adjust
it in the panel, or the reverse. If a deployment composes no settings service the
form renders read-only and says so, rather than accepting a change with nowhere
to put it.

**Installing changes nothing on its own.** Every trigger defaults to on, but no
provider is c

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness bundle: official Microsoft Playwright MCP (@playwright/mcp) - accessibility-tree browser automation for DSH agents
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-playwright

[![Listed on dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org/badges/listed.svg)](https://dsh-plugin.org/plugins/akash-digitavision/dsh-playwright)

**One-line value:** install this and every DeepSeek Harness agent can drive a real browser — navigation, clicking, typing, snapshots, screenshots — using the official Microsoft Playwright MCP.

DeepSeek Harness profile bundle installing the **official Microsoft Playwright MCP** (`@playwright/mcp`) — browser automation through structured **accessibility snapshots** (no vision model needed), from [github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp). Same bundle pattern as `dsh-chrome-devtools`.

**Capability category:** 工具与能力 (Tools & Capabilities)
**License:** MIT · **Compatibility:** DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 (bundles API), Windows/macOS/Linux (Node.js + npx + Chrome/Chromium required)

Configuration source: verified via Context7 against the project's own README — the standard client config is exactly:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "playwright": { "command": "npx", "args": ["@playwright/mcp@latest"] } } }
```

## What it adds to every agent on the profile

| Row | Module | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp-playwright` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` | Spawns `npx @playwright/mcp@latest` (stdio) → tools namespaced `mcp__playwright__*`: `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_take_screenshot`, tabs, requests, and more |

- Uses your **installed Google Chrome** by default (headed, persistent profile)
- First start downloads the package via npx (30–60s); afterwards it starts in ~1s
- Coexists with `dsh-chrome-devtools` — separate tool namespace and browser instance

## Install

**One command (recommended):**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:akash-digitavision/dsh-playwright
```

or in **Settings → Plugin Market** (DSH Plugin Hub), search for `dsh-playwright`.

**Manual alternative** — add `dsh-playwright` to the profile `package.json` `dependencies` + `dsh.profile.bundles`, run `pnpm install` in the profile, restart or re-apply.

**Requirements:** Node.js ≥ 18 with npx (the MCP server downloads on first use), and an installed Chrome or Chromium.

> Note: `file:` dependencies are **copied** into the profile by pnpm — after editing this bundle's `cordis.patch.yml`, run `pnpm install` again (or edit the installed copy under `node_modules\dsh-playwright`) before re-applying.

## Permissions & external services

- Spawns a local `npx @playwright/mcp` process that launches a real browser on your machine
- No accounts, no API keys, no telemetry; network access is whatever pages you browse
- Edits/automation run with your user privileges — review prompts before approving destructive actions

## Optional launch flags

Append to `args` in `cordis.patch.yml`:

| Flag | Effect |
|---|---|
| `--isolated` | In-memory profile; no persisted cookies/storage |
| `--headless` | No visible browser window |
| `--browser chromium` | Playwright's bundled Chromium instead of system Chrome |
| `--caps=vision,pdf` | Extra capability tools |
| `--config <file.json>` | Full JSON configuration (browser, timeouts, network rules, secrets — see project docs) |

## Verify

Ask the agent to `browser_navigate` to any page and `browser_snapshot` it — or check the plugin list for the live `include:mcp-playwright` entry.

## Publish / uninstall

Push this folder to GitHub and install `"dsh-playwright": "github:<you>/dsh-playwright"`. Remove from `bundles` + `dependencies` to uninstall; the npx cache can be kept or cleared separately.

plugins.description: Token usage statistics dashboard plugin for DeepSeek Harness: stat cards, 53-week activity heatmap, per-model trend and model share
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-usage-dashboard

DeepSeek Harness 的 Token 用量统计插件 —— 在 **设置 → Token 统计** 中提供 zcode 风格的用量面板：

- **5 张指标卡**：累计 Token、单日峰值、最长会话时长、当前/最长连续使用天数
- **Token 活动热力图**：53 周 GitHub 风格（每日 / 累计切换）
- **每日 Token 趋势**：近 7 日 / 近 30 日，按模型分系列折线
- **模型用量环形图**：占比 + 明细列表

## 原理

- **零运行时依赖**，图表全部手写 SVG。
- 服务端注册 `tokenStats` 会话投影（`ctx.sessionProjections.register`），
  折叠 `request/header` / `step/start` / `assistant usage` / `step/end` /
  `compaction/summary` 事件，按 **天 × 模型** 累计 token。Harness 会在会话
  首次被触碰时回放持久化日志，因此历史会话同样被统计。
- 客户端通过 `settings.section` 槽位注入设置页，聚合全部会话的
  `projectionValues.tokenStats` 渲染面板。

## 安装

### npm（推荐）

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-usage-dashboard
# 桌面版：设置 → 插件 → Add plugin → npm 包名填 dsh-usage-dashboard
```

### 从源码 / 本地开发

```bash
# web / tui profile：
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-usage-dashboard

# desktop profile 暂无插件页安装入口，需手动：
# 1. 依赖 + bundle 声明（ ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json ）
#    dependencies 增加 "dsh-usage-dashboard": "file:/path/to/dsh-usage-dashboard"
#    dsh.profile.bundles 增加 "dsh-usage-dashboard"
# 2. 安装
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop && npx pnpm@11.9.0 install
# 3. 重启 DeepSeek Harness 应用
```

### 从 GitHub

```bash
dsh plugin add github:<owner>/dsh-usage-dashboard
```

（git 安装装的是源码，可能需要在 profile 的 pnpm-workspace 里授权构建脚本；
优先推荐 npm 安装。）

## 历史数据回填

投影按需折叠：只有被打开过的会话才有数据。要一次性回填全部历史，运行：

```bash
node tools/backfill.mjs --dry   # 预览
node tools/backfill.mjs         # 写入 projcache（自动跳过活跃会话）
```

回填后重启 Harness，设置面板立即显示全部历史统计。

## 口径说明

- token 总量 = input + cacheRead + cacheWrite + output（与内置 tokenUsage 投影一致，
  已对 19 个真实会话逐一对账验证）。
- 同一 (turn, step) 的多次 usage 上报只计最新一次（流式 chunk 替换语义）。
- 不估算费用，只统计 token。

## 开发

```bash
npm run check   # 语法检查
npm test        # 投影 fold 单元测试（node:test，无外部依赖）
```

## 兼容性

peer 依赖接受 DSH `0.1.0-rc.6` 起的 0.1 线与 0.2 线全部版本（含 rc）。
0.3.0 及以后未经测试。

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

plugins.description: 把 DeepSeek Harness 和 WorkBuddy 连起来：记忆/技能同步 + 无界面遥控 + 界面驱动（CDP）+ 对话面板，四合一插件。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-wb —— 让 DeepSeek Harness 和 WorkBuddy 互相认识

![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/YE-ZINAN/dsh-wb?label=release&color=00d4ff)
![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/YE-ZINAN/dsh-wb?color=8b5cf6)
![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows-0078d4)

一句话：装了它，你在 dsh 里就能**看到 WorkBuddy 记了什么、让它干活、跟它对话，甚至直接用 dsh 操作 WorkBuddy 的界面**。

---

## 这是干什么的

WorkBuddy 和 dsh 本来是两套各干各的 AI 工具：各聊各的、各记各的。这个插件把它们连起来 —— 装**一个**插件，多出**四样能力**：

| 你能做的事 | 说白了就是 |
|---|---|
| 📚 **看它记住了什么** | 把 WorkBuddy 的记忆、技能、计划列出来、搜出来、读出来 |
| 🛠️ **让它干活** | 把任务丢给 WorkBuddy 本机的执行引擎，跑完把结果拿回来 |
| 💬 **在 dsh 里跟它聊** | dsh 里多一个「WB 对话」面板，不用来回切窗口 |
| 🖱️ **直接操作它的界面** | 打开它的历史对话、替它发消息 —— **对话留在 WorkBuddy 里**，用它自己的账号额度 |

最后一条是重点：不是"另起一个进程偷偷跑"，而是**真的在 WorkBuddy 界面里操作**。所以你在旁边看着，能看见字一个个打进去。

![在 WorkBuddy 里跑的对话](docs/shots/wb-app.png)

上图是 **WorkBuddy 那边**的样子 —— 对话真的长在它的界面里。

下图是 **dsh 这边**的面板：左边选会话、中间看内容、上面切模型（带积分倍率）。

![dsh 里的 WB 对话面板](docs/shots/dsh-panel.png)

---

## 你需要什么

- **Windows**（目前按 Windows 实现）
- 装好 **dsh 桌面版**
- 装好 **WorkBuddy 桌面版**
- 会点图标就行

---

## 安装

三种方式，挑一种：

**① 一条地址装（推荐，最省事，不需要任何账号）**

在 dsh 的插件管理里「从地址安装」，粘这个：

```
https://github.com/YE-ZINAN/dsh-wb/releases/download/v1.0.0/dsh-wb-1.0.0.tgz
```

（它就是个 npm 包，dsh 会自动下载依赖装好。）

**② 从 GitHub 仓库直接装**

```
github:YE-ZINAN/dsh-wb
```

**③ 本地文件夹**

把仓库下载下来，在插件管理里选那个文件夹。

> **npm**：包名 `dsh-wb` 已确认可用，但本机还没登录 npm（`npm login` 只能你本人做）。
> 你登录后任一时刻执行 `npm publish` 就能发上去 —— 之后大家用 `dsh-wb` 这个包名装即可。

装完 **刷新一次 dsh 页面**（F5），左栏会多一个 WB 图标。

---

## 第一次用

1. 点左栏的 **WB 图标**，打开对话面板
2. 顶上「传输方式」保持 **WB 界面**（这样对话才出现在 WorkBuddy 里）
3. 「会话」下拉选一段历史 → 它会**在 WorkBuddy 里真的切过去**，面板同步显示那段历史
4. 下面输入框打字，回车

> 只想让它后台跑、不碰界面？把「传输方式」切成 **无界面**。

---

## 工作原理（一眼看懂）

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph DSH["dsh · 你的控制台"]
    P["WB 对话面板"]
    T["25 个工具"]
  end
  subgraph WB["WorkBuddy · 真正干活的那个"]
    UI["界面"]
    E["执行引擎"]
    M["记忆 / 技能"]
  end
  P -- 1 --> UI
  T -- 2 --> UI
  T -- 3 --> E
  T -- 4 --> M
```

① HTTP 路由：面板通过宿主的路由直接读写界面内容
② CDP 调试端口：工具在**真实界面**里点击、输入、发送
③ headless 进程：另起一个命令行进程干活（界面里看不到，但最稳）
④ 直接读写文件：同步记忆与技能清单

四块各走各的路，互不影响：

| 模块 | 走哪条路 | 什么时候用它 |
|---|---|---|
| `sync` | 直接读写文件 | 想把两边的记忆和技能清单对齐 |
| `bridge` | 另起一个命令行进程 | 让它稳稳干活（界面里看不到，但最快最省事） |
| `gui` | CDP 调试端口 | 操作真实界面、想看着它干 |
| `chat` | 上面几个的合体 | 就是那个对话面板 |

---

## 安全提醒（请读一遍）

- **调试端口开着的时候，本机上任何程序都能完全控制 WorkBuddy**（读你所有会话、替你发消息）。
  端口只绑 `127.0.0.1`，**手机和局域网进不来**，但本机程序没有门槛。
- 不想长期开着：关掉 WorkBuddy，或下次**不带参数**启动，端口就没了。
- 这个插件**不读你的 API key**。它用的是 WorkBuddy 自己的账号额度；就算你在引擎配置里放了私有 key，本插件也从不读取、不转发。
- 界面模式抓的是界面上的文字，只在你本机流转，不会上传到任何地方。

## 它不会动你的东西

- **不删、不改**你的 WorkBuddy 数据；
- 同步只往你指定的日志文件里**追加**，写前自动备份（`.bak-dshsync`），每次写了什么都有台账可查；
- 身份类信息**永不自动写入**，要你自己确认。

---

## 遇到问题

**面板显示「CDP 未连」**
WorkBuddy 是普通方式启动的，没开调试端口。两个办法：
1. 点面板上的「**启动/重连 WB**」—— 它会关掉并重启 WorkBuddy 并带上端口。会话不会丢（都落盘了）。
2. 一劳永逸：把开始菜单里 WorkBuddy 快捷方式的启动参数改成
   `--remote-debugging-port=9223 --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion`
   以后每次启动都自带端口，最小化时界面也不卡。

**WorkBuddy 最小化时界面好像不动**
Chromium 对最小化窗口会停止重绘 —— 上面那串参数里的后半段就是解决它的。

**对话串到别的会话里了**
早期版本有这个 bug（已修）。如果还遇到，把当时的操作顺序告诉作者。

---

## 想深入了解

- [技术总览](docs/architecture.md)：结构、配置、回滚
- 四个模块的实测细节（含踩过的坑）：[sync](docs/sync.md) · [bridge](docs/bridge.md) · [chat](docs/chat.md) · [gui](docs/gui.md)

## 规模

25 个工具 / 15 条 HTTP 路由 / 1 个对话面板 —— 四个模块合成一个插件。所有测试加起来 **210 项断言**，全绿。

## 许可

MIT

plugins.description: 让 DeepSeek Harness 的 web_fetch 在 Clash/mihomo 的 fake-ip（TUN）下可用：放行 fake-ip 段，仍拒绝回环/内网/云元数据等地址。零依赖 DSH 插件。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-web-fetch-lan

让 DeepSeek Harness 的 `web_fetch` 在 Clash / mihomo 的 **fake-ip** 环境下正常工作：放行 fake-ip 段，同时保留对内网、回环、云元数据等地址的拦截。零依赖，无需构建。

## 它解决什么问题

DSH 的 `web_fetch` 自带 SSRF 防护：连接前先解析域名，只要解析结果里出现非公网地址就直接拒绝，报 `WEB_BLOCKED_URL`：

```
Error: URL hostname "example.com" resolves to a non-public IP address
```

而 Clash / mihomo 开启 TUN + `enhanced-mode: fake-ip` 后，**所有域名都会被解析到保留段**（默认 `198.18.0.0/15` 与 `2001:2::/64`）。这些地址在 `ipaddr.js` 眼里不是 `unicast`，于是所有抓取全被拦下——哪怕你本机上网完全正常。

结果就是：开着 TUN 时 `web_fetch` 几乎不可用，关掉 TUN 才能用。更麻烦的是 Windows 上可能同时向两个网卡查 DNS，一会儿返回 fake-ip、一会儿返回真实 IP，表现为**时好时坏、难以复现**。

## 它做了什么

提供一个替换用的 fetch provider（`id = http-lan`），判定规则只有一处不同：

| 解析结果 | 内置 provider | 本插件 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 公网地址 | 放行 | 放行 |
| fake-ip 段（可配置） | **拒绝** | **放行** |
| 回环 / 私网 / 链路本地 / CGNAT / 组播 / 保留段 | 拒绝 | 拒绝 |

也就是只把「fake-ip 这一段」当作可用：它只在 TUN 内部有意义，连接会被 mihomo 按域名映射转发到你本来要访问的站点，**并不会真的连到 198.18.x.x 那台主机**。而 `127.0.0.1`、`192.168.x.x`、`169.254.169.254`、`[::1]` 等等依旧被挡住，本机服务、内网设备、云元数据端点不会因为装了这个插件而暴露。

顺带修掉一个实测问题：在 TUN + fake-ip 环境下，如果让 Node 按 DNS 原顺序（`verbatim`，IPv6 优先）连接，HTTPS 会**间歇性 `ECONNRESET`**（TCP 通、TLS 阶段被重置），连内置 provider 也躲不过。插件在 `apply()` 里把本进程的 DNS 结果顺序设为 `ipv4first`，实测连续 8/8 成功；这只是排序偏好，没有 A 记录时仍会走 AAAA。

## 安装

插件走 DSH 的插件管理器安装（不是 `dsh plugin` CLI——桌面版 profile 由 Electron 独占管理）：

1. 把本仓库放在任意目录，例如 `D:\repository\dsh-web-fetch-lan`；
2. 打开 DSH 侧栏 **插件** → **添加插件**，填入该目录的**绝对路径**，安装；
3. 若提示需要重启，就重启一次 DSH：provider 是宿主进程启动时装载的。

安装后 profile 的 `package.json` 会多出一条 `link:` 依赖与一个 bundle 条目。要卸载就回到插件页删除，内置 provider 立刻恢复。

> 相对路径会被安装器拒绝，填绝对路径。

## 配置

fake-ip 段在 loader 行的 `config` 里配置，默认值写在 [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml)：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: web-fetch-lan
      name: '@local/dsh-web-fetch-lan'
      config:
        fakeIpRanges:
          - 198.18.0.0/15
        fakeIpRanges6:
          - 2001:2::/64
          - fdfe:dcba:9876::/64
```

在 Clash Verge 里改了 `fake-ip-range` / `fake-ip-range6` 之后，把新段补进这里，重启 DSH 即可，不用改代码。

不想改本仓库文件的话，在 profile 层覆盖（`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`）：

```yaml
- id: web-fetch-lan
  config:
    fakeIpRanges: ['198.18.0.0/15']
    fakeIpRanges6: ['2001:2::/64']
```

容错规则：条目逐个做 CIDR 校验，**非法条目剔除后保留其余**；非数组、或全部非法时**回退内置默认段**并在日志告警——不会因为配置写错而静默放行一切。生效的段会在启动日志里打印一行：

```
[web-fetch-lan] fake-ip 段 v4=198.18.0.0/15 v6=2001:2::/64,fdfe:dcba:9876::/64
```

`cordis.patch.yml` 里另有一条把 `web` 条的 `fetchProvider` 固定为 `http-lan`：内置的 `web-fetch-http` 依然注册着，不显式指定会得到 `WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS`。

## 自检

零依赖，直接跑：

```bash
node selftest.mjs
# 或
pnpm test
```

覆盖配置归一与回退、地址判定、provider 装配，以及 `127.0.0.1` / `169.254.169.254` / `[::1]` / `192.168.3.1` / `file:` / 带凭据 URL 仍被拒绝；末尾附带一次真实抓取（代理没开时只提示，不计入退出码）。

## 边界

与内置 provider 保持一致的行为与限制：

- **仅同源重定向**，最多 5 跳；跨源跳转（含 `http://` → `https://` 的协议升级）会拒绝并提示重试目标 URL；
- 响应上限 2 MiB，正文截断 200,000 字符；只接受文本类 `content-type`；
- 单次抓取 30 秒超时；
- URL 不允许携带凭据，只支持 `http:` / `https:`。

注意区分两种失败：`fetch failed` 是网络层错误（多半是代理节点本身不通），不是被 SSRF 拦截；被拦截时的报错会明确写 `not a public address` / `resolves to a non-public IP address`。

## 目录结构

```
index.js          插件本体：地址判定、抓取实现、apply()
cordis.patch.yml  bundle patch：注册 provider + 插入插件行 + fake-ip 段配置
selftest.mjs      自检脚本（零依赖）
package.json      dsh.bundle.patch 指向 cordis.patch.yml
```

## 许可

[MIT](LICENSE)

plugins.description: Unofficial React components in the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) web UI design system: the DSH primitives plus the components DSH lacks (cards, tabs, pagination, messages, upload, date/time pickers), on the same --dsw-* tokens.
plugins.readme_text:
# @seekbuddy/dsh-ui English | [中文](README.zh.md) React components in the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) web UI design system, for building product pages around DSH: the DSH primitives (`--dsw-*` design tokens, light / dark themes, controls, icons, Markdown and tool-output renderers) plus the components DSH does not provide, such as cards, tabs, pagination, messages, upload and date / time pickers, built on the same tokens. Packaged for ordinary React 18 / 19 and Next.js apps. **Live preview:** every component in [Storybook](https://seekbuddy.github.io/dsh-ui/). > **Unofficial.** This project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by DeepSeek. It ships no DeepSeek brand assets (logo or wordmark). See [THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). ## Why this package The DSH UI primitives (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`) cover what the DSH web shell needs: chat, tool output, menus, dialogs. A product built around DSH also has consoles, settings and admin pages, and those need components DSH does not have: cards, tabs, pagination, date and time input, upload, global messages. Writing them separately in each app drifts away from the DSH look; patching them into a copy of the primitives turns every upstream sync into a merge. This package provides those components and keeps them apart from DSH: - **Extension components** (`@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/seekbuddy`) fill the gaps. They are styled only with the DSH tokens and follow DSH's styling rules, so they sit next to DSH controls without looking different, and they reuse DSH controls through the public entry instead of re-implementing them. See [docs/components](docs/components/README.md). - **The DSH layer** is a copy of the upstream primitives with packaging fixes only, each recorded in [UPSTREAM.md](UPSTREAM.md), so it follows upstream tags. To make the DSH layer usable in an ordinary app, it also fixes three packaging problems of the official package: | Official package | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui` | | --- | --- | | One root entry re-exports everything, so Shiki and KaTeX land in the first page load | Split entries; the root entry is guarded at build time against reaching Markdown, Shiki, KaTeX or the code-file artwork | | Theme tokens and theme switching live in a Cordis plugin | `tokens.css` and a standalone `light / dark / system` theme runtime with a no-flash bootstrap script | | KaTeX output is converted with the browser-only `DOMParser` | SSR-safe KaTeX rendering; tested with React 18 SSR and a Next.js 16 build | ## Install ```sh npm install @seekbuddy/dsh-ui ``` Peer dependencies: `react` and `react-dom` `^18.2.0 || ^19.0.0`. ## Quick start Import the global token sheet once, in your app entry. Import `katex.css` only if you render math. ```tsx import '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/tokens.css' import '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/katex.css' import { Button, Pill } from '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui' import { MarkdownText } from '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/markdown' import { IconCheckOutlineRegular } from '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/icons' import { setThemePreference } from '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/theme' const labels = { code: { copyLabel: 'Copy', copiedLabel: 'Copied' }, footnotes: 'Footnotes', } export function Example() { return (
Enabled
) } ``` Component styles are CSS Modules compiled into the JavaScript and injected into `` once, the first time a component module loads. `tokens.css` and `katex.css` are the only global stylesheets. Components contain no user-facing text: every visible or screen-reader label is a prop (usually a typed `labels` object), so you localize them in your app. ## Entry points Import only from these entries; anything else under `dist/` is internal. | Entry | Contents | | --- | --- | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui` | Lightweight controls and utilities: `Button`, `Input`, `Pill`, `Tag`, `Switch`, `Checkbox`, `Menu`, `MenuSurface`, `Modal`, `Tooltip`, `Toast`, `HoverCard`, `SegmentedControl`, `SegmentedTabs`, positioning / modal hooks, and helpers such as `relativeTime`, `fileSizeText`, `rankByName` | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/blocks` | Tool-output renderers `TerminalBlock`, `ReadBlock`, `DiffBlock`, `SearchBlock`, `WebBlock`, `JsonTree`; file / link icons `FileTypeIcon`, `LinkIconRegular` / `LinkIconMedium`; code highlighting `languageForPath`, `useCodeHighlighter` (loads Shiki) | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/markdown` | `MarkdownText`, `CodeBlock`, `JsonBlock`, `MarkdownDelegateProvider`, `extractMarkdownPlainText` | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/icons` | 188 `Icon*` components (94 glyphs × `Regular` / `Medium` stroke), `PermissionIcon*`, `ReferenceIcon*`, `PluginArtwork*`, `GuideArtwork*` | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/theme` | Theme state, DOM application and React hooks | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/theme/bootstrap` | `THEME_BOOTSTRAP_SCRIPT`, an inline script with no React dependency | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/seekbuddy` | Extra components ([docs](docs/components/README.md)); the whole entry is a Client Component | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/seekbuddy/{card,empty,spinner,timeline}` | Hook-free extra components that a Next.js Server Component may import | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/seekbuddy/tabs` | `Tabs`; same as importing it from `/seekbuddy` | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/tokens.css` | The eight DSH theme sheets, concatenated in their cascade order | | `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/katex.css` | KaTeX CSS reduced to woff2 fonts | ## Two layers | Layer | Source | Contents | | --- | --- | --- | | DSH layer | `src/` except `src/seekbuddy/` | A copy of the DSH web UI primitives and theme sheets, kept in sync with upstream tags. Local changes are listed in [UPSTREAM.md](UPSTREAM.md); everything else is unchanged upstream code. | | Extra components | `src/seekbuddy/` | Components DSH does not provide, written for this package and styled only with `--dsw-*` tokens | Extra components: `Card`, `Empty`, `Mark`, `MessageProvider` + `useMessage`, `Pagination` (+ `pageItems`), `QrCode`, `Spinner`, `StatusBadge`, `Switch`, `Tabs`, `Timeline`, `Upload`, `DangerButton`, `SubtleButton`, and the date / time family `Calendar`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker`, `TimePicker`, `DateField`, `DateRangeField`, `TimeField`. **Each one is documented — usage, examples and the full API — in [docs/components](docs/components/README.md).** The extra components import DSH components through the public `@seekbuddy/dsh-ui` entry, never by relative path. A bundler can therefore alias that entry to another copy of the DSH primitives (for example the one a DSH web shell already loads), and the page keeps a single implementation of each control. Importing one component from `/seekbuddy` does not pull in the others: every component is built into its own chunk, together with its CSS. ## Theme The theme preference is `light | dark | system`. It is stored in `localStorage` under `dsh-ui-primitives.theme-preference` (the key keeps the package's former name for compatibility). ```tsx import { initializeTheme, setThemePreference, useIsDark, useThemePreference } from '@seekbuddy/dsh-ui/theme' initializeTheme() ``` `initializeTheme()` restores a valid stored value and falls back to `system`; it still applies the theme when `localStorage` is unavailable. The theme is applied through `document.documentElement.style.colorScheme` and the `data-ds-dark-theme` attribute on `body`. For server-rendered apps, run the bootstrap script before the page content, so a stored dark preference does not flash light on first load.
